alex_sales: POC kickoff with FinWave tomorrow AM. They want Private deployment into their VPC behind customer firewall + client IP preservation. Need a short checklist (networking, firewall ports), quick pricing ballpark for a 2-week eval, and any BYOL/licensing notes.
joanna_se: @alex_sales good call. Do they want PrivateLink interface endpoints or VPC peering for this POC? That changes the allowlist and whether we require NAT/EIP mapping.
raj_cust: Security team prefers PrivateLink initially. They're open to peering if latency is an issue. Also: absolutely no outbound SNAT that rewrites source IPs.
mike_netops: For PrivateLink: traffic comes from their subnets to our interface endpoint/NLB in their VPC. To preserve client IPs you can: 1) enable proxy-mode (X-Forwarded-For preserved), or 2) use an EIP-mapped NAT on their side so backend sees stable src. If they need original TCP src IP (not header), only peering or EIP-preserved NAT will work.
sara_security: Confirm TLS termination plan. We support TLS passthrough, or terminate at Redwood and use mTLS to customer backend. We can integrate CMK (AWS KMS) or customer HSM for key management, and provide audit logs and SOC2 artifacts.
joanna_se: Quick firewall snippet customers can hand to NetOps: 
``
# Allow from customer subnets to Redwood Privatelink endpoints
ALLOW tcp 443 from <CUSTOMER_CIDR> to 172.31.200.0/24  # privatelink eni range
ALLOW tcp 8443 from <CUSTOMER_CIDR> to 172.31.200.0/24  # health/control plane
# Optional probe
ALLOW icmp from <CUSTOMER_CIDR> to 172.31.200.0/24
```
mike_netops: Operational gotchas: MTU — recommend 1400 for VPN/SD-WAN paths. ARP/proxy-arp — some on-prem appliances send gratuitous ARP that breaks PL health checks; request ARP suppression if you see flapping.
raj_cust: We run an F5 with SIP ALG in the same VPC. Will that break anything? Telephony uses SIP/RTP on separate flows.
mike_netops: SIP ALG can rewrite SNI/TLS or other headers if deep-inspecting. Keep SIP on separate security zones. We do not require SIP ports for inference.
alex_sales: Pricing: do we charge differently for Private POC vs Hosted? Any short-term commit for Dedicated?
joanna_se: We can provide a temporary Dedicated slice for a 2-week Private POC (no annual commit). Ballpark: small POC (1-2 GPU equivalent) ~$3k–$6k for two weeks depending on model/quantization. Egress billed separately ~ $0.10–$0.15/GB. Final quote needs model choice and tokens/sec estimate. I'll produce a one-page quote today.
sara_security: For customer security questionnaire we'll need data classification, retention policy, and CMK requirement. We'll supply SOC2 summary and KMS integration blurb.
joanna_se: Action items: - raj_cust: share VPC CIDRs and NetOps contact (preferred interface-endpoint subnets) - mike_netops: prepare allowlist CIDRs/FQDNs and exact NLB/ENI range we'll allocate - sara_security: attach SOC2 summary and CMK/HSM notes - alex_sales: send POC quote by EOD PST
mike_netops: Healthcheck ports: tcp 8443 and tcp 443. If strict egress ACLs, allow outbound to our region EIP block (we'll provide ephemeral list for POC).
raj_cust: I'll PM NetOps contact and upload firewall export in ~2 hours. Also: confirm whether source IP shows up in app logs over PrivateLink (for fraud detection).
mike_netops: PrivateLink with proxy-mode (X-Forwarded-For) surfaces client IPs in app logs. For original TCP source IP at kernel level you need peering or EIP NAT preserve. We'll document both options in the handoff.
alex_sales: If we get ACLs today can infra stand up the POC by tomorrow morning?
joanna_se: Likely yes, contingent on CIDRs + signed trial agreement. @deploy-bot please reserve a canary slot tomorrow 09:00 PST for a private POC (2-week).
deploy-bot: reserved canary-deploy slot 2024-05-09 09:00 PST for ticket #POC-1983 :white_check_mark:
raj_cust: Thanks all — I'll upload the firewall rules and NetOps contact.
alex_sales: I'll attach the security docs and quote after joanna sends infra request. :thumbsup:
